fills.reason: The only configured WebView (PrivacyPolicyActivity) enables JavaScript but never sets setAllowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs(true); searched all modules for UniversalAccessFromFileURLs and setAllowContentAccess with no hits.
JavaScript is enabled in PrivacyPolicyActivity, but neither setAllowFileAccessFromFileURLs nor setAllowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs is set and minSdk is 24 (≥16), so both stay false.

Password fields use textPassword (login, set-password dialog, public link), the share password toggles between PASSWORD/VISIBLE_PASSWORD with NO_SUGGESTIONS, and passcode digits use android:password with a numeric type; username uses textNoSuggestions.

FLAG_SECURE is set on LoginActivity, PassCodeActivity and PatternActivity, but file lists and previews only get it when MDM disables screenshots (MainApp.kt:122). A human needs to decide whether user file content counts as sensitive by default.

Notifications show no credentials or OTPs, but sync-failure and conflict notifications include the account name (user@server) and remote file paths. With minSdk 24 that is visible on the lock screen; whether this counts as sensitive is a product decision.
Login, link-password and passcode inputs are masked by default (textPassword / android:password). The visible-password mode only appears after the user taps the reveal toggle.
JavaScript is enabled in PrivacyPolicyActivity, but no module calls addJavascriptInterface or uses @JavascriptInterface.
filterTouchesWhenObscured is applied on login, passcode, pattern, sharing, file list and dialogs. It defaults to on (PreferenceUtils returns true unless the user opts out).

Internal startService/bindService/startActivity calls use explicit component Intents. The one broadcast (FileSyncAdapter) goes through LocalBroadcastManager. Implicit intents (ACTION_VIEW/SEND/OPEN_DOCUMENT) only hand off to external, user-chosen apps.

Implicit intents with extras are user-initiated shares (ACTION_SEND of a link or files) or picker intents. Account and credential extras are only put on explicit intents (LoginActivity, ConflictsResolveActivity).
Every PendingIntent.getActivity call uses FLAG_IMMUTABLE and an explicit base intent (LoginActivity, UploadListActivity, SettingsActivity, ConflictsResolveActivity, FileDisplayActivity).
LoginActivity's deep-link filters use the custom schemes 'oc' and 'owncloud' (setup.xml). No http/https deep link is declared, so App Links verification does not apply.

The OAuth redirect handler checks 'state' against the stored oidcState before using 'code'. The owncloud:// deep link is checked against a path-segment format (DeepLinkException) and resolved to a file by remote id only within the user's own accounts.

ReceiveExternalFilesActivity is a SEND share target and LoginActivity is the OAuth redirect/deep-link entry; both are public by design. The passcode/pattern/biometric lock runs for every activity via MainApp onActivityStarted, so starting them directly doesn't bypass the lock.

The exported services are the standard AccountAuthenticator and SyncAdapter bindings. They only return the framework binders (getIBinder / getSyncAdapterBinder), which AccountManager/SyncManager need and which the framework mediates. No custom IPC or sensitive action is exposed.
An OAuth2 client secret is hardcoded in a string resource shipped in the APK and used for token refresh when no dynamically registered secret is stored.

evidence.detail: Hardcoded OAuth2 client secret in resources.

fills.reason: Security values (OAuth state, PKCE verifier, generated link passwords) use SecureRandom. java.util.Random appears only in an unreferenced RandomUtils helper and for a notification thread name.
Time-based values (System.currentTimeMillis) are used only as PendingIntent request codes and notification timestamps, never for tokens, keys or passwords.

The only key is an AndroidKeyStore AES key generated with no explicit setKeySize, so it gets the default (128-bit), which OWASP treats as insufficient. The key encrypts no data (it only gates biometric unlock), so whether this matters is a human call.
The only Cipher/KeyGenerator use is AES (BiometricViewModel). No DES, 3DES, RC4 or Blowfish anywhere.
The only Cipher transformation is AES/CBC/PKCS7Padding. No ECB or bare 'AES' transformation.
No KeyPairGenerator or asymmetric KeyGenParameterSpec anywhere. The only keystore key is symmetric AES.
The only named provider is AndroidKeyStore (KeyStore.getInstance and KeyGenerator.getInstance for a keystore-backed key). No BC or Crypto provider is requested.
The app calls KeyguardManager.isDeviceSecure (LockTimeout.kt) and uses it for the MDM device-protection check.

BiometricPrompt gets a CryptoObject, but the cipher is never used for a cryptographic operation. Success is decided by comparing object references in onAuthenticationSucceeded, so the unlock is event-bound in practice.

evidence.detail: Unlock decided by object comparison in the callback; no encrypt/decrypt with the authenticated cipher.

fills.reason: setInvalidatedByBiometricEnrollment is never called, so the default (true) applies to the biometric key.
PromptInfo sets setConfirmationRequired(true).
The key uses setUserAuthenticationRequired(true) with no setUserAuthenticationParameters or ValidityDurationSeconds, so no extended validity.
No setAllowedAuthenticators, DEVICE_CREDENTIAL or setDeviceCredentialAllowed. The prompt uses a negative (cancel) button, so it is biometric-only.

HttpClient explicitly falls back to SSLContext TLSv1.1/TLSv1.0, and TLSSocketFactory enables TLSv1.1 on sockets. The fallback only runs when TLS 1.2 is unavailable, and TLSSocketFactory has no callers.

evidence.detail: Explicit fallback to TLS 1.1 (then 1.0 on line 112).
TLSv1.1 explicitly enabled on sockets.

fills.reason: When a server is not reachable over TLS, the server base URL is built with http:// and used for all WebDAV/API traffic. The base-config permits cleartext, so these requests go out unencrypted.

evidence.detail: Non-SSL servers get an http:// base URL used for communication.

fills.reason: All HTTPS goes through OkHttp with a hostnameVerifier set. The only raw SSLSocket code (TLSSocketFactory) is never instantiated.

AdvancedX509TrustManager skips all validation (chain, trust and expiry) for any certificate in the 'known servers' store, i.e. self-signed or untrusted certs the user accepted earlier. This deliberately loosens trust.

evidence.detail: Certificates in the known-servers store bypass standard trust and validity checks.

fills.reason: KnownServersHostnameVerifier returns true for any hostname when the peer certificate is in the known-servers store, so a certificate accepted for one server is trusted for every host.

evidence.detail: Hostname mismatch accepted if the certificate is in the known store, regardless of host.

fills.reason: No pin-set in network_security_config.xml, and code 'pinning' is only user-accepted certificates in the known-servers store. The app talks mostly to user-chosen self-hosted servers, so which endpoints are under the developer's control and need pinning is a product decision.
